Terminal Algo Trading must be ON when CAS is expected to place, modify, or close MT5 demo orders and learn from broker acceptance, fills, slippage, rejection, stop-loss, and take-profit outcomes. With Algo Trading OFF, CAS may still observe real broker quotes and completed candles, but it cannot collect genuine MT5 execution outcomes. The AI Operator reviews each exact fresh RouteIntent candidate and decides APPROVE or STAND_DOWN and, when approving, controls lot size by selecting one exact sizing_ref from broker-valid PROBE, STANDARD, PRESS_EDGE, and MAX_WITHIN_ENVELOPE choices. Those choices are calculated from stop risk, equity, free margin, margin utilization, portfolio exposure, broker minimum, maximum and lot step, and owner caps. Approval is an executable entry decision, not an advisory label: the selected exact order continues through order_dispatch.py, execution_guard.py, and the selected broker bridge without per-order human confirmation. The model cannot invent a free-form volume or rewrite symbol, direction, entry, stop-loss, take-profit, strategy, or decision identity. A daily profit-target deficit is never sizing authority. The Operator cannot resurrect a deterministic rejection or bypass any authority, risk, broker-truth, duplicate, recovery, or kill-switch gate. A paper-lane model outage may use the explicit degraded paper policy; a live-lane model or contract failure requires STAND_DOWN.
Model failure may degrade only on PAPER under explicit policy; LIVE model failure must STAND_DOWN.
The immediate AI Operator chooses one exact sizing_ref or STAND_DOWN. The broker minimum is an available floor, not a permanent lot size.
The broker minimum is an available floor, not a permanent 0.01-lot policy; execution_guard.py recalculates at broker touch.

Every immediate APPROVE or STAND_DOWN prompt must include current account balance, equity, margin, open positions, combined paper learning, the broker-verified MT5 demo subset, and candidate-specific realized outcomes for the same symbol, direction, and strategy. The prompt and durable report retain a context hash. One broker close observed through multiple audit paths counts once by broker_ticket plus decision_ref; richer metadata is merged rather than double-counted. Sparse evidence remains explicitly sparse. A prior loss requires materially differentiated regime or strategy evidence before repeated sampling, but one loss is not a permanent veto.
Broker-outcome binder and candidate-specific prompt context.
Deduplicate one broker close observed through multiple provenance paths.

Open-position management is not merely a fixed-rule subsystem labeled AI. Fresh broker position and quote truth first produce deterministic, broker-valid management drafts. The immediate AI Operator then selects one exact discretionary action per broker position or returns STAND_DOWN using current account truth, all open positions, owner guidance, owner-fenced controls, and realized outcome history. The model cannot rewrite broker ticket, symbol, side, volume, stop-loss, take-profit, or action identity. Exact scale_in drafts are first-class discretionary actions. They are generated only for a fresh, protected parent whose open P&L is net positive after every currently reported swap, carry, and commission amount; each sizing option is broker-grid valid and carries current stop risk, margin, parent ticket, unit index, sizing_ref, and sizing-plan hash. The Operator may select one add without per-add human confirmation. Its short-lived authorization is account/config/parent/order bound and one-shot. A pre-cost winner that is net losing after reported costs, stale parent, changed parent volume or protective geometry, reused authorization, cap breach, or unrecognized sizing_ref blocks before broker touch. Current quote, open-P&L, cost, account, position, candidate, guidance, control, and outcome evidence are bound into the decision cache identity.
